children.text: nidhāya hṛdi viśveśaṃ vidhāya guruvandanam /
children.translated_text: Having placed the Lord of the Universe in the heart, and having performed obeisance to the teacher,

children.text: bālānāṃ sukhabodhāya kriyate tarkasaṃgrahaḥ //
children.translated_text: this <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> (Compendium of Logic) is composed for the easy understanding of beginners.

children.text: nidhāya hṛdi viśveśaṃ vidhāya guru-vandanam /
bālānāṃ sukha-bodhāya kriyate tarka-saṃgrahaḥ //

body.text: dravyaguṇakarmasāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyābhāvāḥ sapta padārthāḥ //
body.translated_text: The seven categories (<s>padārthas</s>) are: substance (<s>dravya</s>), quality (<s>guṇa</s>), action (<s>karma</s>), universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), particularity (<s>viśeṣa</s>), inherence (<s>samavāya</s>), and absence (<s>abhāva</s>).

children.text: dravya-guṇa-karma-sāmānya-viśeṣa-samavāya-abhāvāḥ sapta pada-arthāḥ //

body.text: tatra dravyāṇi pṛthivyaptejovāyvākāśakāladigātmamanāṃsi navaiva //
body.translated_text: Among these, the substances are nine only: earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>), water (<s>ap</s>), fire (<s>tejas</s>), air (<s>vāyu</s>), space (<s>ākāśa</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), direction (<s>dik</s>), self (<s>ātman</s>), and mind (<s>manas</s>).

children.text: tatra dravyāṇi pṛthivy-ap-tejo-vāyv-ākāśa-kāla-dig-ātma-manāṃsi nava-eva //

body.text: rūparasagandhasparśasaṃkhyāparimāṇapṛthaktvasaṃyogavibhāgaparatvāparatvagurutvadravatvasnehaśabdabuddhisukhaduḥkhecchādveṣaprayatnadharmādharmasaṃskārāś caturviṃśati guṇāḥ //
body.translated_text: The twenty-four qualities are: color (<s>rūpa</s>), taste (<s>rasa</s>), smell (<s>gandha</s>), touch (<s>sparśa</s>), number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>), magnitude (<s>parimāṇa</s>), separateness (<s>pṛthaktva</s>), conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), disjunction (<s>vibhāga</s>), remoteness (<s>paratva</s>), proximity (<s>aparatva</s>), heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>), fluidity (<s>dravatva</s>), viscosity (<s>sneha</s>), sound (<s>śabda</s>), cognition (<s>buddhi</s>), pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), desire (<s>icchā</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), effort (<s>prayatna</s>), merit (<s>dharma</s>), demerit (<s>adharma</s>), and dispositional tendency (<s>saṃskāra</s>).

children.text: rūpa-rasa-gandha-sparśa-saṃkhyā-parimāṇa-pṛthaktva-saṃyoga-vibhāga-paratva-aparatva-gurutva-dravatva-sneha-śabda-buddhi-sukha-duḥkha-icchā-dveṣa-prayatna-dharma-adharma-saṃskārāś caturviṃśati guṇāḥ //

body.text: utkṣepaṇāvakṣepaṇākuñcanaprasāraṇagamanāni pañca karmāṇi //
body.translated_text: The five actions (<s>karmāṇi</s>) are: throwing upward (<s>utkṣepaṇa</s>), throwing downward (<s>avakṣepaṇa</s>), contraction (<s>ākuñcana</s>), expansion (<s>prasāraṇa</s>), and locomotion (<s>gamana</s>).

children.text: utkṣepaṇa-avakṣepaṇa-ākuñcana-prasāraṇa-gamanāni pañca karmāṇi //

body.text: param aparaṃ ceti dvividhaṃ sāmānyam //
body.translated_text: Universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) is of two kinds: higher (<s>para</s>) and lower (<s>apara</s>).

children.text: param aparaṃ ca iti dvividhaṃ sāmānyam //

body.text: nityadravyavṛttayo viśeṣās tv anantā eva //
body.translated_text: Particularities (<s>viśeṣas</s>), which reside in eternal substances, are indeed infinite in number.

children.text: nitya-dravya-vṛttayo viśeṣās tv an-antā eva //

body.text: samavāyas tv eka eva //
body.translated_text: Inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) is indeed one only.

children.text: samavāyas tv eka eva //

body.text: abhāvaś caturvidhaḥ / prāgabhāvaḥ pradhvaṃsābhāvo 'tyantābhāvo 'nyonyābhāvaś ceti //
body.translated_text: Absence (<s>abhāva</s>) is of four kinds: prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>), posterior absence (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>), absolute absence (<s>atyantābhāva</s>), and mutual absence (<s>anyonyābhāva</s>).

children.text: abhāvaś caturvidhaḥ / prāg-abhāvaḥ pradhvaṃsa-abhāvo 'tyanta-abhāvo 'nyonya-abhāvaś ca iti //

body.text: gandhavatī pṛthivī / sā dvividhā nityānityā ca / nityā paramāṇurūpā / anityā kāryarūpā / punas trividhā śarīrendriyaviṣayabhedāt / śarīram asmadādīnām / indriyaṃ gandhagrāhakaṃ ghrāṇaṃ nāsāgravarti / viṣayo mṛtpāṣāṇādiḥ //
body.translated_text: Earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) is that which possesses smell (<s>gandha</s>). It is of two kinds: eternal and non-eternal. The eternal is in the form of atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>). The non-eternal is in the form of effects (<s>kārya</s>). The latter is again of three kinds, distinguished as body, sense-organ, and object. The body is that of ourselves and others. The sense-organ is the organ of smell (<s>ghrāṇa</s>), which apprehends smell and is located at the tip of the nose. The objects are earth, stone, and the like.

children.text: gandhavatī pṛthivī / sā dvividhā nitya-anityā ca / nityā paramāṇu-rūpā / anityā kārya-rūpā / punas trividhā śarīra-indriya-viṣaya-bhedāt / śarīram asmad-ādīnām / indriyaṃ gandha-grāhakaṃ ghrāṇaṃ nāsa-agravarti / viṣayo mṛt-pāṣāṇa-ādiḥ //

body.text: śitasparśavatya āpaḥ / tā dvividhāḥ nityā anityāś ca / ntyāḥ paramāṇurūpāḥ / anityāḥ kāryarūpāḥ. / punas trividhāḥ. śarīrendriyaviṣayabhedāt / śarīraṃ varuṇaloke / indriyaṃ rasagrāhakaṃ rasanaṃ jihvāgravarti / viṣayaḥ saritsamudrādiḥ //
body.translated_text: Water (<s>āpas</s>) is that which possesses cold touch. It is of two kinds: eternal and non-eternal. The eternal is in the form of atoms. The non-eternal is in the form of effects. The latter is again of three kinds, distinguished as body, sense-organ, and object. The body is in the world of <s>Varuṇa</s>. The sense-organ is the tongue (<s>rasana</s>), which apprehends taste and is located at the tip of the tongue. The objects are rivers, oceans, and the like.

children.text: śita-sparśavatya āpaḥ / tā dvividhāḥ nityā anityāś ca / ntyāḥ paramāṇu-rūpāḥ / anityāḥ kārya-rūpāḥ. / punas trividhāḥ. śarīra-indriya-viṣaya-bhedāt / śarīraṃ varuṇa-loke / indriyaṃ rasa-grāhakaṃ rasanaṃ jihva-agravarti / viṣayaḥ sarit-samudra-ādiḥ //

body.text: uṣṇasparśavat tejaḥ / tad dvividhaṃ nityam anityaṃ ca / niyyaṃ paramāṇurūpam / anityaṃ kāryarūpam / punas trividhaṃ śarīrendriyaviṣayabhedāt / śarīram ādityaloke / indriyaṃ rūpagrāhakaṃ cakṣuḥ kṛṣṇatārāgravarti / viṣayaś caturvidhaḥ / bhaumadivyaudaryākarajabhedāt / bhaumaṃ vahnyādikam / abindhanaṃ divyaṃ vidyudādi / bhuktasya pariṇāmahetur audaryam. ākarajaṃ suvarṇādi //
body.translated_text: Fire (<s>tejas</s>) is that which possesses hot touch. It is of two kinds: eternal and non-eternal. The eternal is in the form of atoms. The non-eternal is in the form of effects. The latter is again of three kinds, distinguished as body, sense-organ, and object. The body is in the world of the sun (<s>Āditya</s>). The sense-organ is the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>), which apprehends color, and is located at the dark pupil of the eye. The object is of four kinds, distinguished as terrestrial (<s>bhauma</s>), celestial (<s>divya</s>), digestive (<s>audarya</s>), and mineral (<s>ākaraja</s>). The terrestrial is fire and the like. The celestial, which is without fuel, is lightning and the like. The digestive is the cause of the transformation of what has been eaten. The mineral is gold and the like.

children.text: uṣṇa-sparśavat tejaḥ / tad dvividhaṃ nityam anityaṃ ca / niyyaṃ paramāṇu-rūpam / anityaṃ kārya-rūpam / punas trividhaṃ śarīra-indriya-viṣaya-bhedāt / śarīram ādityaloke / indriyaṃ rūpa-grāhakaṃ cakṣuḥ kṛṣṇatāra-agravarti / viṣayaś caturvidhaḥ / bhauma-divya-audarya-ākaraja-bhedāt / bhaumaṃ vahny-ādikam / abindhanaṃ divyaṃ vidyud-ādi / bhuktasya pariṇāma-hetur audaryam. ākarajaṃ suvarṇa-ādi //

body.text: rūparahitasparśavān vāyuḥ / sa dvividho nityo 'nityaś ca / nityaḥ paramāṇurūpaḥ / anityaḥ kāryarūpaḥ / punas trividhaḥ śarīrendriyaviṣayabhedāt / śarīraṃ vāyuloke / indriyaṃ sparśagrāhakaṃ tvaksarvaśarīravarti / viṣayo vṛkṣādikampanahetuḥ // śarīrāntaḥsaṃcārī vāyuḥ prāṇaḥ / sa caiko 'py upādhibhedāt prāṇāpānādisaṃjñā labhate //
body.translated_text: Air (<s>vāyu</s>) is that which possesses touch but is devoid of color. It is of two kinds: eternal and non-eternal. The eternal is in the form of atoms. The non-eternal is in the form of effects. The latter is again of three kinds, distinguished as body, sense-organ, and object. The body is in the world of air (<s>Vāyu</s>). The sense-organ is the skin (<s>tvak</s>), which apprehends touch and pervades the entire body. The object is that which causes the shaking of trees and the like. The air that circulates within the body is called <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath). And though it is one, it receives the designations <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and so forth due to the difference in limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>).

children.text: rūpa-rahita-sparśavān vāyuḥ / sa dvividho nityo 'nityaś ca / nityaḥ paramāṇu-rūpaḥ / anityaḥ kārya-rūpaḥ / punas trividhaḥ śarīra-indriya-viṣaya-bhedāt / śarīraṃ vāyu-loke / indriyaṃ sparśa-grāhakaṃ tvak-sarva-śarīravarti / viṣayo vṛkṣa-ādi-kampana-hetuḥ // śarīra-antaḥsaṃcārī vāyuḥ prāṇaḥ / sa ca eko 'py upādhi-bhedāt prāṇa-apāna-ādi-saṃjñā labhate //

body.text: śabdaguṇam ākāśam / tac caikaṃ vibhu nityaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: Space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is that which has sound as its quality. And it is one, all-pervading (<s>vibhu</s>), and eternal.

children.text: śabda-guṇam ākāśam / tac ca ekaṃ vibhu nityaṃ ca //

body.text: atītādivyavahārahetuḥ kālaḥ / sa caiko vibhur nityaś ca //
body.translated_text: Time (<s>kāla</s>) is the cause of the usage of 'past' and the like. And it is one, all-pervading, and eternal.

children.text: atīta-ādi-vyavahāra-hetuḥ kālaḥ / sa ca eko vibhur nityaś ca //

body.text: prācyādivyavahārahetur dik / sā caikā vibhvī nityā ca //
body.translated_text: Direction (<s>dik</s>) is the cause of the usage of 'eastern' and the like. And it is one, all-pervading, and eternal.

children.text: prācya-ādi-vyavahāra-hetur dik / sā ca ekā vibhvī nityā ca //

body.text: jñānādhikaraṇam ātmā / sa dvividhaḥ paramātmā jīvātmā ca / tatreśvaraḥ sarvajñaḥ paramātmaika eva / jīvātmā pratiśarīraṃ bhinno vibhur nityaś ca //
body.translated_text: The self (<s>ātman</s>) is the substratum of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). It is of two kinds: the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) and the individual self (<s>Jīvātman</s>). Among these, <s>Īśvara</s> (God), the omniscient one, the Supreme Self, is one alone. The individual self is distinct for each body, all-pervading, and eternal.

children.text: jñāna-adhikaraṇam ātmā / sa dvividhaḥ param-ātmā jīva-ātmā ca / tatrā iśvaraḥ sarvajñaḥ param-ātmā-eka eva / jīva-ātmā pratiśarīraṃ bhinno vibhur nityaś ca //

body.text: sukhādyupalabdhisādhanam indriyaṃ manaḥ / tac ca pratyātmaniyatatvād anantaṃ paramāṇurūpaṃ nityaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: The mind (<s>manas</s>) is the instrument for the apprehension of pleasure and the like. And since it is restricted to each individual self, [the minds are] infinite [in number]; it is of atomic size and eternal.

children.text: sukha-ādy-upalabdhi-sādhanam indriyaṃ manaḥ / tac ca pratyātma-niyatatvād anantaṃ paramāṇu-rūpaṃ nityaṃ ca //

body.text: cakṣurmātragrāhyo guṇo rūpam / tac ca śuklanīlapītaraktaharitakapiśacitrabhedāt saptavidhaṃ pṛthivījalatejovṛtti / tatra pṛthivyāṃ saptavidham / abhāsvaraśuklaṃ jale / bhāsvaraśuklaṃ tejasi //
body.translated_text: Color (<s>rūpa</s>) is a quality apprehended by the eye alone. It is of seven kinds, distinguished as white, blue, yellow, red, green, brown, and variegated. It resides in earth, water, and fire. In earth, it is of all seven kinds. In water, it is non-luminous white. In fire, it is luminous white.

children.text: cakṣur-mātra-grāhyo guṇo rūpam / tac ca śukla-nīla-pīta-rakta-harita-kapiśa-citra-bhedāt saptavidhaṃ pṛthivī-jala-tejo-vṛtti / tatra pṛthivyāṃ saptavidham / abhāsvara-śuklaṃ jale / bhāsvara-śuklaṃ tejasi //

body.text: rasanagrāhyo guṇo rasaḥ / sa ca madhurāmlalavaṇakaṭukaṣāyatiktabhedāt ṣaḍvidhaḥ / pṛthivyāṃ ṣaḍvidhaḥ / jale madhura eva //
body.translated_text: Taste (<s>rasa</s>) is a quality apprehended by the tongue. It is of six kinds, distinguished as sweet, sour, salty, pungent, astringent, and bitter. In earth, it is of all six kinds. In water, it is sweet alone.

children.text: rasana-grāhyo guṇo rasaḥ / sa ca madhu-rāmla-lavaṇa-kaṭu-kaṣāya-tikta-bhedāt ṣaḍvidhaḥ / pṛthivyāṃ ṣaḍvidhaḥ / jale madhura eva //

body.text: ghrāṇagrāhyo guṇo gandhaḥ / sa ca dvividhaḥ surabhirasurabhiś ca / pṛthivīmātravṛttiḥ /
body.translated_text: Smell (<s>gandha</s>) is a quality apprehended by the nose. It is of two kinds: pleasant (<s>surabhi</s>) and unpleasant (<s>asurabhi</s>). It resides in earth alone.

children.text: ghrāṇa-grāhyo guṇo gandhaḥ / sa ca dvividhaḥ surabhir-asurabhiś ca / pṛthivī-mātra-vṛttiḥ /

body.text: tvagindriyamātragrāhyo guṇo saparśaḥ / sa ca trividhaḥ śitoṣṇānuṣṇāśītabhedāt / pṛthivyaptejovāyuvṛttiḥ / tatra śīto jale / uṣṇas tejasi / anuṣṇāśītaḥ pṛthivīvāyvoḥ //
body.translated_text: Touch (<s>sparśa</s>) is a quality apprehended by the skin-organ alone. It is of three kinds, distinguished as cold, hot, and neither-cold-nor-hot. It resides in earth, water, fire, and air. Cold [touch] is in water. Hot [touch] is in fire. Neither-cold-nor-hot [touch] is in earth and air.

children.text: tvag-indriya-mātra-grāhyo guṇo saparśaḥ / sa ca trividhaḥ śita-uṣṇa-anuṣṇa-aśīta-bhedāt / pṛthivy-ap-tejo-vāyu-vṛttiḥ / tatra śīto jale / uṣṇas tejasi / anuṣṇa-aśītaḥ pṛthivī-vāyvoḥ //

body.text: rūpādicatuṣṭayaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pākajam anityaṃ ca / anyatrāpākajaṃ nityam antyaṃ ca / nityagataṃ nityam / anityagatam anityam //
body.translated_text: The group of four — color, taste, smell, and touch — in earth is produced by heat (<s>pākaja</s>) and is non-eternal. Elsewhere [in water, fire, and air], it is not produced by heat and is eternal or non-eternal: that which resides in what is eternal is eternal; that which resides in what is non-eternal is non-eternal.

children.text: rūpa-ādi-catuṣṭayaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pākajam anityaṃ ca / anyatra apākajaṃ nityam antyaṃ ca / nityagataṃ nityam / anityagatam anityam //

body.text: ekatvādivyavahārahetuḥ saṃkhyā / navadravyavṛttir ekatvādiparārdhaparyantā / ekatvaṃ nityam anityaṃ ca / nityagataṃ nityam anityagatam anityam / dvitvādikaṃ tu sarvatrānityam eva //
body.translated_text: Number (<s>saṃkhyā</s>) is the cause of the usage of 'one' and the like. It resides in [all] nine substances and ranges from oneness to the highest count (<s>parārdha</s>). Oneness is eternal or non-eternal: that in what is eternal is eternal; that in what is non-eternal is non-eternal. But duality and the rest are always non-eternal everywhere.

children.text: ekatva-ādi-vyavahāra-hetuḥ saṃkhyā / nava-dravya-vṛttir ekatva-ādi-parārdha-paryantā / ekatvaṃ nityam anityaṃ ca / nityagataṃ nityam anityagatam anityam / dvitva-ādikaṃ tu sarvatra a-nityam eva //

body.text: mānavyavahārakāraṇaṃ parimāṇaṃ / navadravyavṛtti / tac caturvidham / aṇu mahad dīrghaṃ hrasvaṃ ceti //
body.translated_text: Magnitude (<s>parimāṇa</s>) is the cause of the usage of measurement. It resides in [all] nine substances. It is of four kinds: atomic (<s>aṇu</s>), great (<s>mahat</s>), long (<s>dīrgha</s>), and short (<s>hrasva</s>).

children.text: māna-vyavahāra-kāraṇaṃ parimāṇaṃ / nava-dravya-vṛtti / tac caturvidham / aṇu mahad dīrghaṃ hrasvaṃ ca iti //

body.text: pṛthagvyavahārakāraṇaṃ pṛthagtvaṃ / sarvadravyavṛtti //
body.translated_text: Separateness (<s>pṛthaktva</s>) is the cause of the usage of 'separate.' It resides in all substances.

children.text: pṛthag-vyavahāra-kāraṇaṃ pṛthagtvaṃ / sarvadravyavṛtti //

body.text: saṃyuktavyavahārahetuḥ saṃyogaḥ / sarvadravyavṛttiḥ //
body.translated_text: Conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>) is the cause of the usage of 'conjoined.' It resides in all substances.

children.text: saṃyukta-vyavahāra-hetuḥ saṃyogaḥ / sarvadravyavṛttiḥ //

body.text: saṃyoganāśako guṇo vibhāgaḥ / sarvadravyavṛttiḥ //
body.translated_text: Disjunction (<s>vibhāga</s>) is the quality that destroys conjunction. It resides in all substances.

children.text: saṃyoga-nāśako guṇo vibhāgaḥ / sarvadravyavṛttiḥ //

body.text: parāparavyavahārāsādhāraṇakāraṇe paratvāparatve / pṛthivyādicatuṣṭayamanovṛttīti / te dvividhe dikkṛte kālakṛte ca / dūrasthe dikkṛtaṃ paratvam / samīpasthe dikkṛtam aparatvam / jyeṣṭhe kālakṛthaṃ paratvam / kaniṣṭhe kālakṛtam aparatvam //
body.translated_text: Remoteness (<s>paratva</s>) and proximity (<s>aparatva</s>) are the uncommon causes of the usage of 'remote' and 'proximate.' They reside in the group of four — earth and the rest [i.e., earth, water, fire, air] — and in mind. They are of two kinds: produced by direction and produced by time. Remoteness produced by direction is in what is far away. Proximity produced by direction is in what is nearby. Remoteness produced by time is in what is older. Proximity produced by time is in what is younger.

children.text: para-apara-vyavahāra-asādhāraṇa-kāraṇe paratva-aparatve / pṛthivy-ādi-catuṣṭaya-mano-vṛtti iti / te dvividhe dik-kṛte kāla-kṛte ca / dūra-sthe dik-kṛtaṃ paratvam / samīpasthe dik-kṛtam aparatvam / jyeṣṭhe kāla-kṛthaṃ paratvam / kaniṣṭhe kāla-kṛtam aparatvam //

body.text: ādyapatanāsamavāyikāraṇaṃ gurutvaṃ / pṛthivījalavṛtti //
body.translated_text: Heaviness (<s>gurutva</s>) is the non-inherent cause of the initial falling [of an object]. It resides in earth and water.

children.text: ādya-patana-asamavāyi-kāraṇaṃ gurutvaṃ / pṛthivī-jala-vṛtti //

body.text: ādyasyandanāsamavāyikāraṇaṃ dravatvaṃ pṛthivyaptejovṛtti / tad dvividhaṃ sāṃsiddhikaṃ naimittikaṃ ca / sāṃsiddhikaṃ jale naimittikaṃ pṛthivītejasoḥ / pṛthivyāṃ ghṛtādāvagnisaṃyogajanyaṃ daravatvam / tejasi suvarṇādau //
body.translated_text: Fluidity (<s>dravatva</s>) is the non-inherent cause of the initial flowing. It resides in earth, water, and fire. It is of two kinds: natural (<s>sāṃsiddhika</s>) and incidental (<s>naimittika</s>). The natural is in water. The incidental is in earth and fire. In earth, fluidity produced by contact with fire occurs in ghee and the like. In fire, it occurs in gold and the like.

children.text: ādya-syandana-asamavāyi-kāraṇaṃ dravatvaṃ pṛthivy-ap-tejo-vṛtti / tad dvividhaṃ sāṃsiddhikaṃ naimittikaṃ ca / sāṃsiddhikaṃ jale naimittikaṃ pṛthivī-tejasoḥ / pṛthivyāṃ ghṛta-ādāv-agni-saṃyogajanyaṃ daravatvam / tejasi suvarṇādau //

body.text: cūrṇādipiṇḍībhāvahetur guṇaḥ snehaḥ / jalamātravṛttiḥ //
body.translated_text: Viscosity (<s>sneha</s>) is the quality that is the cause of the formation of a lump from powder and the like. It resides in water alone.

children.text: cūrṇa-ādi-piṇḍī-bhāva-hetur guṇaḥ snehaḥ / jala-mātra-vṛttiḥ //

body.text: śrotragrāhyo guṇaḥ śabdaḥ / ākāśamātravṛttiḥ / sa dvividho dvanyātmako varṇātmakaś ceti / dvanyātmako bheryādau / varṇātmakaḥ saṃskṛtabhāṣādirūpaḥ //
body.translated_text: Sound (<s>śabda</s>) is a quality apprehended by the ear. It resides in space (<s>ākāśa</s>) alone. It is of two kinds: that which is of the nature of a resonance (<s>dhvani</s>) and that which is of the nature of a phoneme (<s>varṇa</s>). The resonance-type is in drums and the like. The phoneme-type has the form of Sanskrit language and the like.

children.text: śrotra-grāhyo guṇaḥ śabdaḥ / ākāśa-mātra-vṛttiḥ / sa dvividho dvany-ātmako varṇa-ātmakaś ca iti / dvany-ātmako bhery-ādau / varṇa-ātmakaḥ saṃskṛta-bhāṣā-ādi-rūpaḥ //

body.text: sarvavyavahārahetur buddhir jñānam / sā dvividhā smṛtiranubhavaś ca / saṃskāramātrajanyaṃ jñānaṃ smṛtiḥ / tadbhinnaṃ jñānam anubhavaḥ //
body.translated_text: Cognition (<s>buddhi</s>), which is knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), is the cause of all practical activity. It is of two kinds: memory (<s>smṛti</s>) and experience (<s>anubhava</s>). Knowledge produced solely from dispositional impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is memory. Knowledge other than that is experience.

children.text: sarva-vyavahāra-hetur buddhir jñānam / sā dvividhā smṛtir-anubhavaś ca / saṃskāra-mātra-janyaṃ jñānaṃ smṛtiḥ / tad-bhinnaṃ jñānam anubhavaḥ //

body.text: sa dvividho yathārtho 'yathārthaś ca / tadvati tatprakārako 'nubhavo yathārthaḥ / yathā rajata idaṃ rajatam iti jñānam / sa eva pramety ucyate / tadabhāvavati tatprakārako 'nubhavo 'yathārthaḥ / yathā śuktāv idaṃ rajatam iti jñānam //
body.translated_text: Experience is of two kinds: veridical (<s>yathārtha</s>) and non-veridical (<s>ayathārtha</s>). An experience that qualifies something by a qualifier that actually belongs to it is veridical — for example, the cognition 'this is silver' with respect to [actual] silver. That is also called valid knowledge (<s>pramā</s>). An experience that qualifies something by a qualifier that does not belong to it is non-veridical — for example, the cognition 'this is silver' with respect to shell.

children.text: sa dvividho yathārtho 'yathārthaś ca / tad-vati tat-prakārako 'nubhavo yathārthaḥ / yathā rajata idaṃ rajatam iti jñānam / sa eva prama īty ucyate / tad-abhāva-vati tat-prakārako 'nubhavo 'yathārthaḥ / yathā śuktāv idaṃ rajatam iti jñānam //

body.text: yathārthānubhavaś caturvidhaḥ pratyakṣānumityupamitiśabdabhedāt / tatkaraṇam api caturvidhaṃ pratyakṣānumānopamānaśabdabhedāt //
body.translated_text: Veridical experience is of four kinds, distinguished as perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumiti</s>), comparison (<s>upamiti</s>), and verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>). Their instruments (<s>karaṇas</s>) are also of four kinds, distinguished as perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), comparison (<s>upamāna</s>), and verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>).

children.text: yathārtha-anubhavaś caturvidhaḥ pratyakṣa-anumity-upamiti-śabda-bhedāt / tat-karaṇam api caturvidhaṃ pratyakṣa-anumāna-upamāna-śabda-bhedāt //

body.text: asādhāraṇam kāraṇaṃ karaṇam /
body.translated_text: An uncommon cause is called an instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>).

children.text: asādhāraṇam kāraṇaṃ karaṇam /

body.text: kāryaniyatapūrvavṛtti kāraṇam /
body.translated_text: A cause (<s>kāraṇa</s>) is that which invariably precedes the effect and is fixed [in relation to it].

children.text: kārya-niyata-pūrva-vṛtti kāraṇam /

body.text: kāryaṃ prāgabhāvapratiyogi /
body.translated_text: An effect (<s>kārya</s>) is the counter-correlate of prior absence (<s>prāgabhāva</s>).

children.text: kāryaṃ prāg-abhāva-pratiyogi /

body.text: kāraṇaṃ trividhaṃ samavāyyasamavāyinimittabhedāt / yat samavetaṃ kāryam utpadyate tat samavāyikāraṇam / yathā tantavaḥ paṭasya paṭaś ca khagatarūpādeḥ / kāryeṇa kāraṇena vā sahaikasminn arthe samavetatve sati yat kāraṇaṃ tad asamavāyikāraṇam / yathā tantusaṃyogaḥ paṭasya tanturūpaṃ paṭarūpasya / tadubhayabhinnaṃ kāraṇaṃ nimittakāraṇam / yathā turīvemādikaṃ paṭasya /
body.translated_text: A cause is of three kinds, distinguished as inherent cause (<s>samavāyi</s>), non-inherent cause (<s>asamavāyi</s>), and efficient cause (<s>nimitta</s>). That in which the effect is produced as inhering is the inherent cause — for example, the threads are [the inherent cause] of cloth, and cloth is [the inherent cause] of the color residing in cloth. That which, while being inherent in the same entity as the effect or as the [inherent] cause, is a cause, is the non-inherent cause — for example, the conjunction of threads is [the non-inherent cause] of cloth, and the color of threads is [the non-inherent cause] of the color of cloth. A cause that is different from both of these is the efficient cause — for example, the shuttle, loom, and the like are [the efficient causes] of cloth.

children.text: kāraṇaṃ trividhaṃ samavāyy-asamavāyi-nimitta-bhedāt / yat samavetaṃ kāryam utpadyate tat samavāyikāraṇam / yathā tantavaḥ paṭasya paṭaś ca khagata-rūpādeḥ / kāryeṇa kāraṇena vā saha ekasminn arthe samavetatve sati yat kāraṇaṃ tad asamavāyikāraṇam / yathā tantusaṃyogaḥ paṭasya tanturūpaṃ paṭarūpasya / tad-ubhaya-bhinnaṃ kāraṇaṃ nimittakāraṇam / yathā turī-vema-ādikaṃ paṭasya /

body.text: tad etattrividhakāraṇamadhye yad asādhāraṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ tad eva karaṇam //
body.translated_text: Among these three kinds of causes, that which is the uncommon cause is alone the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>).

children.text: tad etat-trividha-kāraṇa-madhye yad asādhāraṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ tad eva karaṇam //

body.text: tatra pratyakṣajñānakaraṇaṃ pratyakṣam / indriyārthasannikarṣajanyaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣam /tad dvividhaṃ nirvikalpakaṃ savikalpakaṃ ceti / tatra nirvikalpakaṃ jñānaṃ nirvikalpakaṃ yathedaṃ kiṃcit / saparakārakaṃ jñānaṃ savikalpakaṃ yathā ḍittho'yam brahmaṇo'yaṃ śyāmo'yam iti //
body.translated_text: The instrument of perceptual knowledge is perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). Knowledge produced from the contact of a sense-organ with its object is perceptual (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). It is of two kinds: indeterminate (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>) and determinate (<s>savikalpaka</s>). Indeterminate knowledge is of the form 'this is something' [without qualifying characteristics]. Knowledge that has a qualifier is determinate — for example, 'this is <s>Ḍitthaḥ</s>,' 'this is a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,' 'this is dark-complexioned.'

children.text: tatra pratyakṣa-jñāna-karaṇaṃ pratyakṣam / indriya-artha-sannikarṣa-janyaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣam /tad dvividhaṃ nirvikalpakaṃ savikalpakaṃ ca iti / tatra nirvikalpakaṃ jñānaṃ nirvikalpakaṃ yatha īdaṃ kiṃcit / saparakārakaṃ jñānaṃ savikalpakaṃ yathā ḍittho'yam brahmaṇo'yaṃ śyāmo'yam iti //

body.text: pratyakṣajñānahetur indriyārthasannikarṣaḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ / saṃyogaḥ saṃyuktasamavāyaḥ saṃyuktasamavetasamavāyaḥ samavāyaḥ samavetasamavāyo viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaś ceti / cakṣuṣā ghaṭapratyakṣajanane saṃyogaḥ sannikarṣaḥ / ghaṭarūpapratyakṣajanane saṃyuktasamavāyaḥ sannikarṣaḥ cakṣuḥsaṃyukte ghaṭe rūpasya samavāyāt / rūpatvasāmānyapratyakṣe saṃyuktasamavetasamavāyaḥ sannikarṣaḥ cakṣuḥsaṃyukte ghaṭe rūpaṃ samavetaṃ tatra rūpatvasya samavāyāt / śrotreṇa śabdasyākāśaguṇatvāt guṇaguṇinoś ca samavāyāt / śabdatvasākṣātkāre samavetasamavāyaḥ sannikarṣaḥ śrotrasamavete śabde śabdatvasya samavāyāt / abhāvaparatyakṣe viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvaḥ sannikarṣo ghaṭābhāvavad bhṛtalam ity atra cakṣuḥsaṃyukte bhūtale ghaṭābhāvasya viśeṣaṇatvāt / evaṃ snnikarṣaṣaṭkajanyaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣam / tatkaraṇam indriyam / tasmād indriyaṃ pratyakṣapramāṇam iti siddham //
body.translated_text: The cause of perceptual knowledge — the contact between a sense organ and its object (<s>indriyārthasannikarṣa</s>) — is sixfold: <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction), <s>saṃyuktasamavāya</s> (inherence in what is conjoined), <s>saṃyuktasamavetasamavāya</s> (inherence in what inheres in the conjoined), <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), <s>samavetasamavāya</s> (inherence in what inheres), and <s>viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāva</s> (qualifier-qualified relation). In the generation of perception of a pot by the eye, conjunction is the contact. In the generation of perception of the color of a pot, inherence-in-the-conjoined is the contact, since color inheres in the pot which is conjoined with the eye. In the perception of the universal 'colorness,' inherence-in-what-inheres-in-the-conjoined is the contact, since color inheres in the pot conjoined with the eye, and colorness inheres in that color. In hearing sound by the ear, since sound is a quality of <s>ākāśa</s> (space) and since quality and substance stand in the relation of inherence, [the contact is inherence]. In the direct cognition of 'soundness,' inherence-in-what-inheres is the contact, since soundness inheres in the sound that inheres in the ear. In the perception of absence, the qualifier-qualified relation is the contact, as in 'the ground possesses the absence of a pot,' since in the ground conjoined with the eye, the absence of the pot functions as a qualifier. Thus, the cognition generated by the six types of contact is perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). Its instrument is the sense organ (<s>indriya</s>). Therefore it is established that the sense organ is the means of valid perceptual knowledge (<s>pratyakṣa pramāṇa</s>).

children.text: pratyakṣa-jñāna-hetur indriya-artha-sannikarṣaḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ / saṃyogaḥ saṃyukta-samavāyaḥ saṃyukta-samaveta-samavāyaḥ samavāyaḥ samaveta-samavāyo viśeṣaṇa-viśeṣya-bhāvaś ca iti / cakṣuṣā ghaṭa-pratyakṣa-janane saṃyogaḥ sannikarṣaḥ / ghaṭa-rūpa-pratyakṣa-janane saṃyukta-samavāyaḥ sannikarṣaḥ cakṣuḥsaṃyukte ghaṭe rūpasya samavāyāt / rūpatva-sāmānyapratyakṣe saṃyukta-samaveta-samavāyaḥ sannikarṣaḥ cakṣuḥ-saṃyukte ghaṭe rūpaṃ samavetaṃ tatra rūpatvasya samavāyāt / śrotreṇa śabdasyā akāśa-guṇatvāt guṇa-guṇinoś ca samavāyāt / śabdatva-sākṣātkāre samaveta-samavāyaḥ sannikarṣaḥ śrotra-samavete śabde śabdatvasya samavāyāt / abhāvaparatyakṣe viśeṣaṇa-viśeṣya-bhāvaḥ sannikarṣo ghaṭa-abhāvavad bhṛtalam ity atra cakṣuḥ-saṃyukte bhūtale ghaṭa-abhāvasya viśeṣaṇatvāt / evaṃ snnikarṣa-ṣaṭka-janyaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣam / tatkaraṇam indriyam / tasmād indriyaṃ pratyakṣa-pramāṇam iti siddham //

body.text: anumitikaraṇam anumānam / parāmarśajanyaṃ jñānam anumitiḥ / vyāptiviśiṣṭapakṣadharmatājñānaṃ parāmarśaḥ / yathā vahnivyāpyadhūmavān ayaṃ parvata iti jñānaṃ parāmarśaḥ / taj janyaṃ parvato vahnimān iti jñānam anumitiḥ / yatra yatra dhūmas tatrāgnir iti sāhacaryaniyamo vyāptiḥ / vyāpyasya parvatādivṛttitvaṃ pakṣadharmatā //
body.translated_text: The instrument of inferential knowledge is inference (<s>anumāna</s>). The cognition produced by <s>parāmarśa</s> (subsumptive reflection) is inferential knowledge (<s>anumiti</s>). Knowledge of the property of the locus (<s>pakṣadharmatā</s>) as qualified by the universal concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>) is <s>parāmarśa</s>. For example, the cognition 'this mountain possesses smoke, which is pervaded by fire' is <s>parāmarśa</s>. The cognition generated by it — 'the mountain possesses fire' — is <s>anumiti</s>. The invariable co-occurrence 'wherever there is smoke, there is fire' is <s>vyāpti</s> (universal concomitance). The occurrence of the <s>vyāpya</s> (pervaded, i.e., smoke) in the mountain etc. is the <s>pakṣadharmatā</s> (property-of-the-locus).

children.text: anumiti-karaṇam anumānam / parāmarśajanyaṃ jñānam anumitiḥ / vyāpti-viśiṣṭa-pakṣa-dharmatā-jñānaṃ parāmarśaḥ / yathā vahni-vyāpya-dhūmavān ayaṃ parvata iti jñānaṃ parāmarśaḥ / taj janyaṃ parvato vahnimān iti jñānam anumitiḥ / yatra yatra dhūmas tatra agnir iti sāhacarya-niyamo vyāptiḥ / vyāpyasya parvata-ādi-vṛttitvaṃ pakṣadharmatā //

body.text: anumānaṃ dvividhaṃ svārthaṃ parārthaṃ ca / tatra svārthaṃ svānumitihetuḥ / tathā hi svayam eva bhūyo darśanena yatra dhūmas tatra agnir iti mahānasādau vyāptiṃ gṛhītvā parvatasamīpaṃ gatas tadgate cāgnau sandihānaḥ parvate dhūmaṃ paśyan vyāptiṃ smarati yatra dhūmas tatrāgnir iti / tadantaraṃ vahnivyāpyadhūmavān ayaṃ parvata iti jñānam utpadyate / ayam eva liṅgaparāmarṣaṃ ity ucyate / tasmāt parvato vahnimān iti jñānam anumitir utpadyate / tad etat svārthānumānam / yat tu svayaṃ dhūmād agnim anumāya parapratipattyarthaṃ pañcāvayavavākyaṃ prayukte tat parārthānumānam / yathā parvato vahnimān dhūmavattvāt / yo yo dhūmavān sa vahnimān yathā mahānasaḥ / tathā cāyam / tasmāt tatheti / anena pratipāditāl lingāt paro'py agniṃ pratipadyate //
body.translated_text: Inference is twofold: for oneself (<s>svārtha</s>) and for another (<s>parārtha</s>). Of these, inference-for-oneself is the cause of one's own inferential knowledge. Thus: having oneself grasped, through repeated observation, the concomitance 'wherever there is smoke there is fire' in the kitchen etc., having gone near a mountain and being in doubt about the fire on it, seeing smoke on the mountain, one recalls the concomitance: 'wherever there is smoke there is fire.' Thereafter the cognition arises: 'this mountain possesses smoke which is pervaded by fire.' This alone is called the <s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s> (subsumptive reflection on the probans). From that, the inferential cognition arises: 'the mountain possesses fire.' This is inference-for-oneself. But when, having oneself inferred fire from smoke, one employs a five-membered statement for the understanding of another, that is inference-for-another (<s>parārthānumāna</s>). For example: 'The mountain possesses fire, because it possesses smoke. Whatever possesses smoke possesses fire, like a kitchen. And so is this [mountain]. Therefore it is so.' Through the probans thus demonstrated, the other person also ascertains fire.

children.text: anumānaṃ dvividhaṃ sva-arthaṃ para-arthaṃ ca / tatra sva-arthaṃ sva-anumiti-hetuḥ / tathā hi svayam eva bhūyo darśanena yatra dhūmas tatra agnir iti mahānasādau vyāptiṃ gṛhītvā parvatasamīpaṃ gatas tad-gate ca agnau sandihānaḥ parvate dhūmaṃ paśyan vyāptiṃ smarati yatra dhūmas tatra agnir iti / tad-antaraṃ vahni-vyāpya-dhūmavān ayaṃ parvata iti jñānam utpadyate / ayam eva liṅgaparāmarṣaṃ ity ucyate / tasmāt parvato vahnimān iti jñānam anumitir utpadyate / tad etat sva-artha-anumānam / yat tu svayaṃ dhūmād agnim anumāya para-pratipatty-arthaṃ pañca-avayava-vākyaṃ prayukte tat para-artha-anumānam / yathā parvato vahnimān dhūmavattvāt / yo yo dhūmavān sa vahnimān yathā mahānasaḥ / tathā ca-ayam / tasmāt tatha īti / anena pratipāditāl lingāt paro'py agniṃ pratipadyate //

body.text: pratijñāhetūdāharaṇopanayanigamāni pañcāvayavaḥ / parvato vahnimān iti pratijñā / dhūmavattvād iti hetuḥ / yo yo dhūmavān sa so'gnimān yathā mahānasa ity udāharaṇam / tathā cāyam iti upanayaḥ / tasmāt tatheti nigamanam //
body.translated_text: Thesis (<s>pratijñā</s>), reason (<s>hetu</s>), example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>), application (<s>upanaya</s>), and conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>) are the five members (<s>avayavas</s>). 'The mountain possesses fire' is the thesis. 'Because it possesses smoke' is the reason. 'Whatever possesses smoke possesses fire, like a kitchen' is the example. 'And so is this [mountain]' is the application. 'Therefore it is so' is the conclusion.

children.text: pratijñā-hetu-udāharaṇa-upanaya-nigamāni pañca-avayavaḥ / parvato vahnimān iti pratijñā / dhūmavattvād iti hetuḥ / yo yo dhūmavān sa so'gnimān yathā mahānasa ity udāharaṇam / tathā ca ayam iti upanayaḥ / tasmāt tatha īti nigamanam //

body.text: svārthānumitiparārthānumityor liṅgaparāmarśa eva karaṇam / tasmāl liṅgaparāmarśā'numānam //
body.translated_text: In both inference-for-oneself and inference-for-another, the <s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s> (subsumptive reflection on the probans) alone is the instrument. Therefore the <s>liṅgaparāmarśa</s> is inference (<s>anumāna</s>).

children.text: sva-artha-anumiti-para-artha-anumityor liṅga-parāmarśa eva karaṇam / tasmāl liṅga-parāmarśā'numānam //

body.text: liṅgaṃ trividham / anvayavyatireki kevalānvayi kevalavyatireki ceti / anvayena vyatirekeṇa ca vyāptimad anvayavyatireki / yathā vahnau sādhye dhūmavattvam / yatra dhūmas tatrāgnir yathā mahānasa ity anvayavyāptiḥ / yatra vahnir nāsti tatra dhūmo'pi nāsti yathā mahāhrada iti vyatirekavyāptiḥ / anvayamātravyāptikaṃ kevalānvayi yathā ghaṭo'bhidheyaḥ prameyatvāt paṭavat / atra prameyatvābhidhyatvayor vyatirekavyāptir nāsti sarvasyāpi prameyatvād abhidheyatvāc ca / vyatirekamātravyāptikaṃ kevalavyatireki yathā pṛthivī tarebhyo bhidyate gandhavattvāt / yad itarebhyo na bhidyate na tad gandhavat / yathā jalam / na ceyaṃ tathā / tasmān na tatheti atra yad gandhavat tad itarabhinnam ity anvayadṛṣṭanto nāsti pṛthivīmātrasya pakṣatvāt //
body.translated_text: The probans (<s>liṅga</s>) is threefold: <s>anvayavyatirekin</s> (positively and negatively concomitant), <s>kevalānvayin</s> (only positively concomitant), and <s>kevalavyatirekin</s> (only negatively concomitant). That which possesses concomitance both positively and negatively is <s>anvayavyatirekin</s>. For example, when fire is to be proved, 'possession of smoke': 'wherever there is smoke there is fire, like a kitchen' is the positive concomitance; 'where there is no fire there is no smoke, like a large lake' is the negative concomitance. That which has only positive concomitance is <s>kevalānvayin</s>. For example: 'the pot is nameable, because it is knowable, like a cloth.' Here there is no negative concomitance between knowability and nameability, since everything is both knowable and nameable. That which has only negative concomitance is <s>kevalavyatirekin</s>. For example: 'earth differs from the other [elements] because it possesses smell. Whatever does not differ from the others does not possess smell, like water. And this [earth] is not so. Therefore it is not so.' Here there is no positive example — 'whatever possesses smell differs from the others' — since earth alone, being the locus, is the <s>pakṣa</s> (subject).

children.text: liṅgaṃ trividham / anvaya-vyatireki kevala-anvayi kevala-vyatireki ca iti / anvayena vyatirekeṇa ca vyāptimad anvaya-vyatireki / yathā vahnau sādhye dhūmavattvam / yatra dhūmas tatra agnir yathā mahānasa ity anvaya-vyāptiḥ / yatra vahnir na asti tatra dhūmo'pi na asti yathā mahāhrada iti vyatireka-vyāptiḥ / anvaya-mātra-vyāptikaṃ kevala-anvayi yathā ghaṭo'bhidheyaḥ prameyatvāt paṭavat / atra prameyatva-abhidhyatvayor vyatirekavyāptir na asti sarvasya api prameyatvād abhidheyatvāc ca / vyatirekamātravyāptikaṃ kevala-vyatireki yathā pṛthivī tarebhyo bhidyate gandhavattvāt / yad itarebhyo na bhidyate na tad gandhavat / yathā jalam / na ca iyaṃ tathā / tasmān na tatha īti atra yad gandhavat tad itara-bhinnam ity anvayadṛṣṭanto na asti pṛthivī-mātrasya pakṣatvāt //

body.text: saṃdigdhasādhyavān pakṣaḥ / yathā dhūmavattve hetau parvataḥ //
body.translated_text: That which has the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) as doubtful is the <s>pakṣa</s> (subject). For example, where smoke-possession is the reason, the mountain [is the <s>pakṣa</s>].

children.text: saṃdigdha-sādhyavān pakṣaḥ / yathā dhūmavattve hetau parvataḥ //

body.text: niścitasādhyavān sapakṣaḥ / yathā tatraiva mahānasaḥ //
body.translated_text: That which has the <s>sādhya</s> as ascertained [to be present] is the <s>sapakṣa</s> (homologue). For example, in the same [case], the kitchen.

children.text: niścita-sādhyavān sapakṣaḥ / yathā tatra eva mahānasaḥ //

body.text: niścitasādhyābhāvavān vipakṣaḥ / yathā tatraiva mahāhradaḥ //
body.translated_text: That which has the ascertained absence of the <s>sādhya</s> is the <s>vipakṣa</s> (heterologue). For example, in the same [case], the large lake.

children.text: niścita-sādhya-abhāvavān vipakṣaḥ / yathā tatra eva mahāhradaḥ //

body.text: savyabhicāraviruddhasatpakṣāsiddhabādhitāḥ pañca hetvābhāsāḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>savyabhicāra</s> (deviant), <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory), <s>satpratipakṣa</s> (counter-balanced), <s>asiddha</s> (unestablished), and <s>bādhita</s> (contradicted) are the five pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsas</s>).

children.text: savyabhicāra-viruddha-satpakṣa-asiddha-bādhitāḥ pañca hetvābhāsāḥ //

body.text: savyabhicāro'naikāntikaḥ / sa trividhaḥ / sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇānupasaṃhāribhedāt / tatra sādhyābhāvavadvṛttiḥ sādhāraṇo anaikāntikaḥ / yathā parvato vahnimān prameyatvād iti prameyatvasya vahnyabhāvavati hrade vidyamānatvāt / sarvasapakṣavipakṣavyāvṛtto'sādhāraṇaḥ / yathā śabdo nityaḥ śabdatvād iti / śabdatvaṃ sarvebhyo nityebhyo'ntyebhyaś ca vyāvṛttaṃ śabdamātravṛtti / anvayavyatirekadṛṣṭāntarahito'nupasaṃhārī / yathā sarvam anityaṃ prameyatvād iti / atra sarvasyāpi pakṣatvād dṛṣṭānto nāsti //
body.translated_text: The deviant (<s>savyabhicāra</s>) is the inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). It is threefold, due to the distinction between <s>sādhāraṇa</s> (common), <s>asādhāraṇa</s> (uncommon), and <s>anupasaṃhārin</s> (non-conclusive). Of these, that which occurs in what possesses the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> is the common inconclusive. For example, 'the mountain possesses fire because it is knowable' — since knowability exists in the lake where fire is absent. That which is excluded from all homologues and heterologues is the uncommon [inconclusive]. For example, 'sound is eternal because it possesses soundness' — soundness, being present only in sound, is excluded from all eternal and non-eternal things. That which lacks both positive and negative examples is the non-conclusive. For example, 'everything is non-eternal because it is knowable' — here, since everything is the <s>pakṣa</s>, there is no example.

children.text: savyabhicāro'naikāntikaḥ / sa trividhaḥ / sādhāraṇa-asādhāraṇa-anupasaṃhāri-bhedāt / tatra sādhya-abhāvavad-vṛttiḥ sādhāraṇo anaikāntikaḥ / yathā parvato vahnimān prameyatvād iti prameyatvasya vahny-abhāvavati hrade vidyamānatvāt / sarva-sapakṣa-vipakṣa-vyāvṛtto'sādhāraṇaḥ / yathā śabdo nityaḥ śabdatvād iti / śabdatvaṃ sarvebhyo nityebhyo'ntyebhyaś ca vyāvṛttaṃ śabda-mātra-vṛtti / anvaya-vyatireka-dṛṣṭānta-rahito'nupasaṃhārī / yathā sarvam anityaṃ prameyatvād iti / atra sarvasya api pakṣatvād dṛṣṭānto na asti //

body.text: sādhyābhāvavyāpto hetur viruddhaḥ / yatra śabdo nityaḥ kṛtakatvād iti / kṛtakatvaṃ hi nityatvābhāvenānityatvena vyāptam //
body.translated_text: A reason pervaded by the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> is contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>). For example, 'sound is eternal because it is produced' — for 'being produced' is pervaded by the absence of eternality, i.e., by non-eternality.

children.text: sādhya-abhāva-vyāpto hetur viruddhaḥ / yatra śabdo nityaḥ kṛtakatvād iti / kṛtakatvaṃ hi nityatva-abhāvena a-nityatvena vyāptam //

body.text: yasya sādhyabhāvasādhakaṃ hetvantaraṃ vidyate sa satpratipakṣaḥ / yathā śabdo nityaḥ śrāvaṇatvāc chabdatvavad iti / śabdo'nityaḥ kāryatvād ghaṭavad iti //
body.translated_text: That which has another reason that establishes the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> is counter-balanced (<s>satpratipakṣa</s>). For example: 'sound is eternal because it is audible, like soundness' — [but:] 'sound is non-eternal because it is a product, like a pot.'

children.text: yasya sādhya-bhāva-sādhakaṃ hetv-antaraṃ vidyate sa satpratipakṣaḥ / yathā śabdo nityaḥ śrāvaṇatvāc chabdatvavad iti / śabdo'nityaḥ kāryatvād ghaṭavad iti //

body.text: asiddhas trividhaḥ / āśrayāsiddhaḥ svarūpāsiddho vyāpyatvāsiddhaś ceti / āśrayāsiddho yathā gaganāravindaṃ surabhy aravindatvāt sarojāravindavat / atra gaganāravindam āśrayaḥ / sa ca nāsty eva / svarūpāsiddho yathā śabdo guṇaś cākṣuṣatvāt / atra cākṣuṣatvaṃ śabde nāsti śabdasya śrāvaṇatvāt / sopādhiko vyāpyatvāsiddhaḥ / sādhyavyāpakatve sati sādhanāvyāpaka upādhiḥ / sādhyasamānādhikaraṇātyantābhāvāpratiyogitvaṃ sādhyavyāpakatvam / sādhanavann iṣṭātyantābhāvapratiyogitvaṃ sādhāraṇāvyapakatvam / parvato dhūmavān vahnimattvād ity atrārdrendhasaṃyoga upādhiḥ / tathā hi / yatra dhūmas tatrārdrendhnasaṃyoga iti sādhyavyāpakatā / yatra vahnis tatrārdrendhanasaṃyogābhāvād iti sādhanāvyāpakatā / evaṃ sādhyavyāpakatve sati sādhanāvyāpakatvād ardrendhanasaṃyoga upādhiḥ / sopādhikatvād vahnimattvaṃ vyāpyatvāsiddham //
body.translated_text: The unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>) is threefold: <s>āśrayāsiddha</s> (unestablished locus), <s>svarūpāsiddha</s> (unestablished in itself), and <s>vyāpyatvāsiddha</s> (unestablished as pervaded). Unestablished-locus: for example, 'the sky-lotus is fragrant because of being a lotus, like a pond-lotus' — here the locus, the sky-lotus, simply does not exist. Unestablished-in-itself: for example, 'sound is a quality visible to the eye because of being a quality' — here visibility-to-the-eye does not exist in sound, since sound is audible. The conditionally-pervaded is unestablished-as-pervaded. A condition (<s>upādhi</s>) is that which pervades the <s>sādhya</s> while not pervading the <s>sādhana</s> (reason). Pervading the <s>sādhya</s> means being the non-counterpositive of a constant absence co-located with the <s>sādhya</s>. Not pervading the <s>sādhana</s> means being the counterpositive of a desired constant absence possessing the <s>sādhana</s>. In 'the mountain possesses smoke because it possesses fire,' contact with wet fuel is the condition. Thus: 'wherever there is smoke there is contact with wet fuel' — this is pervading the <s>sādhya</s>. 'Where there is fire there is absence of contact with wet fuel' — this is not pervading the <s>sādhana</s>. Thus, since [wet fuel contact] pervades the <s>sādhya</s> while not pervading the <s>sādhana</s>, contact with wet fuel is a condition. Because of being conditional, the fact that fire possesses [smoke] is unestablished-as-pervaded.

children.text: asiddhas trividhaḥ / āśraya-asiddhaḥ svarūpa-asiddho vyāpyatva-asiddhaś ca iti / āśraya-asiddho yathā gagana-aravindaṃ surabhy aravindatvāt saro-ja-aravindavat / atra gagana-aravindam āśrayaḥ / sa ca na asty eva / svarūpa-asiddho yathā śabdo guṇaś cākṣuṣatvāt / atra cākṣuṣatvaṃ śabde na asti śabdasya śrāvaṇatvāt / sa-upādhiko vyāpyatva-asiddhaḥ / sādhya-vyāpakatve sati sādhana-avyāpaka upādhiḥ / sādhya-samāna-adhikaraṇa-atyanta-abhāva-apratiyogitvaṃ sādhya-vyāpakatvam / sādhanavann iṣṭa-atyanta-abhāva-pratiyogitvaṃ sādhāraṇa-avyapakatvam / parvato dhūmavān vahnimattvād ity atrā ardra-indhasaṃyoga upādhiḥ / tathā hi / yatra dhūmas tatrā ardra-indhna-saṃyoga iti sādhya-vyāpakatā / yatra vahnis tatrā ardra-indhana-saṃyoga-abhāvād iti sādhana-avyāpakatā / evaṃ sādhya-vyāpakatve sati sādhana-avyāpakatvād ardra-indhana-saṃyoga upādhiḥ / sa-upādhikatvād vahnimattvaṃ vyāpyatva-asiddham //

body.text: yasya sādhyābhāvaḥ pramāṇāntareṇa niścitaḥ sa bādhitaḥ / yathā vahnir anuṣṇo dravyatvād iti / atrānuṣṇatvaṃ sādhyaṃ tadabhāva uṣṇatvaṃ spārśanapratyakṣeṇa gṛhyata iti bādhitatvam //
body.translated_text: That whose <s>sādhya</s>-absence is ascertained by another means of valid knowledge is contradicted (<s>bādhita</s>). For example, 'fire is non-hot because it is a substance.' Here, the <s>sādhya</s> is non-hotness, and its absence — namely hotness — is grasped through tactile perception. Hence it is contradicted.

children.text: yasya sādhya-abhāvaḥ pramāṇa-antareṇa niścitaḥ sa bādhitaḥ / yathā vahnir anuṣṇo dravyatvād iti / atra anuṣṇatvaṃ sādhyaṃ tad-abhāva uṣṇatvaṃ spārśana-pratyakṣeṇa gṛhyata iti bādhitatvam //

body.text: upamitikaraṇam upamānam / saṃjñāsaṃjñisaṃbandhajñānam upamitiḥ / tatkaraṇaṃ sādṛśyajñānam / atideśavākyārthasmaraṇam avāntaravyāpāraḥ / tathā hi kaś cid gavayaśabdārtham ajānan kutaś cid āraṇyakapuruṣād gosadṛśo gavaya iti śrutvā vanaṃ gato vākyārthaṃ smaran gosadṛṣaṃ piṇḍaṃ paśyati / tadanantaram asau gavayaśabdavācya ity upamitir utpadyte //
body.translated_text: The instrument of knowledge-by-comparison is comparison (<s>upamāna</s>). Knowledge of the relation between a name and the named thing is <s>upamiti</s> (comparative knowledge). Its instrument is knowledge of similarity. The intermediary operation is the remembrance of the meaning of the statement of comparison. Thus: someone who does not know the meaning of the word '<s>gavaya</s>' (wild ox), having heard from some forest-dweller that 'a <s>gavaya</s> is similar to a cow,' goes to the forest, remembers the meaning of the statement, and sees an animal similar to a cow. Thereupon the comparative knowledge arises: 'this is what is denoted by the word <s>gavaya</s>.'

children.text: upamiti-karaṇam upamānam / saṃjñā-saṃjñi-saṃbandha-jñānam upamitiḥ / tat-karaṇaṃ sādṛśya-jñānam / atideśa-vākya-artha-smaraṇam avāntara-vyāpāraḥ / tathā hi kaś cid gavaya-śabda-artham ajānan kutaś cid āraṇyaka-puruṣād go-sadṛśo gavaya iti śrutvā vanaṃ gato vākya-arthaṃ smaran go-sadṛṣaṃ piṇḍaṃ paśyati / tad-anantaram asau gavaya-śabda-vācya ity upamitir utpadyte //

body.text: āptavākyaṃ śabdaḥ / āptas tu yathārthavaktā / vākyaṃ padasamūhaḥ / yathā gām ānayeti / śaktaṃ padam / asmāt padād ayam artho boddhavya itīśvarasaṃketaḥ śaktiḥ //
body.translated_text: The sentence of a reliable person is verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>). A reliable person (<s>āpta</s>) is one who speaks what is true. A sentence (<s>vākya</s>) is a collection of words. For example, 'bring the cow.' A word with denotative power is a <s>pada</s> (significant word). Denotative power (<s>śakti</s>) is the convention established by <s>Īśvara</s> (God) that 'from this word, this meaning is to be understood.'

children.text: āpta-vākyaṃ śabdaḥ / āptas tu yatha ārtha-vaktā / vākyaṃ pada-samūhaḥ / yathā gām ānaya iti / śaktaṃ padam / asmāt padād ayam artho boddhavya itī iśvara-saṃketaḥ śaktiḥ //

body.text: ākāṅkṣā yogyatā saṃnidhiś ca vākyārthajñānahetuḥ / padasya padāntaravyatirekaprayuktānvayānanubhāvakatvam ākāṅkṣā / arthābādho yogyatā / padānāmavilambenoccāraṇaṃ saṃnidhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>), compatibility (<s>yogyatā</s>), and contiguity (<s>saṃnidhi</s>) are the causes of sentence-meaning cognition. Expectancy is the incapacity of a word to produce a connected meaning without another word. Compatibility is the absence of contradiction among the meanings. Contiguity is the utterance of words without undue delay.

children.text: ākāṅkṣā yogyatā saṃnidhiś ca vākya-artha-jñāna-hetuḥ / padasya pada-antara-vyatireka-prayukta-anvaya-ananubhāvakatvam ākāṅkṣā / artha-abādho yogyatā / padānām-avilambena uccāraṇaṃ saṃnidhiḥ //

body.text: ākāṅkṣādirahitaṃ vākyam apramāṇam / yathā gaur aśvaḥ puruṣo hastīti na pramāṇam ākāṅkṣāvirahāt / agninā siñced iti na pramāṇaṃ yogyatāvirahāt / prahare prehare'sahoccāritāni gām ānayetyādipadāni na pramāṇaṃ saṃnidhyabhāvāt //
body.translated_text: A sentence lacking expectancy etc. is not a valid means of knowledge. For example, 'cow horse man elephant' is not valid due to the absence of expectancy. 'One should sprinkle with fire' is not valid due to the absence of compatibility. The words 'bring the cow' etc., uttered at intervals of many hours and not together, are not valid due to the absence of contiguity.

children.text: ākāṅkṣā-ādi-rahitaṃ vākyam apramāṇam / yathā gaur aśvaḥ puruṣo hasti īti na pramāṇam ākāṅkṣā-virahāt / agninā siñced iti na pramāṇaṃ yogyatā-virahāt / prahare prehare-'saha uccāritāni gām ānaya ity-ādi-padāni na pramāṇaṃ saṃnidhy-abhāvāt //

body.text: vākyaṃ dvividham / vaidikaṃ laukikaṃ ca / vaidikam īśvaroktatvāt sarvam eva pramāṇam / laukikaṃ tv āptoktaṃ pramāṇam / anyad apramāṇam //
body.translated_text: Sentences (<s>vākya</s>) are of two kinds: Vedic and worldly. Vedic [sentences], being spoken by <s>Īśvara</s> (God), are all authoritative. Worldly [sentences], when spoken by a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>), are authoritative; otherwise, they are non-authoritative.

children.text: vākyaṃ dvividham / vaidikaṃ laukikaṃ ca / vaidikam īśvara-uktatvāt sarvam eva pramāṇam / laukikaṃ tv āpta-uktaṃ pramāṇam / anyad apramāṇam //

body.text: vākyārthajñānaṃ śabdajñānam / tatkaraṇaṃ śabdaḥ //
body.translated_text: The cognition of the meaning of a sentence is verbal knowledge (<s>śabda-jñāna</s>). Its instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) is the word (<s>śabda</s>).

children.text: vākya-artha-jñānaṃ śabda-jñānam / tat-karaṇaṃ śabdaḥ //

body.text: ayathārthānubhavas trividhaḥ saṃśayaviparyayatarkabhedāt / ekasmin dharmini viruddhanānādharmavaiśiṣṭyāvagāhi jñānaṃ saṃśayaḥ / yathā sthāṇur vā purṣo veti / mithyājñānaṃ viparyayaḥ / yathā śuktāv idaṃ rajatam iti / vyāpyāropeṇa vyāpakāropas tarkaḥ yathā yadi vahnir na syāt tarhi dhūmo'pi na syād iti //
body.translated_text: Non-veridical cognition (<s>ayathārtha-anubhava</s>) is of three kinds, being divided into doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), error (<s>viparyaya</s>), and hypothetical reasoning (<s>tarka</s>). A cognition that apprehends contradictory and multiple attributes in a single substrate is doubt — for example, 'Is it a post or a person?' False knowledge is error — for example, 'This is silver' [when seeing a shell]. <s>Tarka</s> (hypothetical reasoning) is the supposition of the pervader through the supposition of the pervaded — for example, 'If there were no fire, then there would be no smoke either.'

children.text: ayathā-artha-anubhavas trividhaḥ saṃśaya-viparyaya-tarka-bhedāt / ekasmin dharmini viruddha-nānā-dharma-vaiśiṣṭya-avagāhi jñānaṃ saṃśayaḥ / yathā sthāṇur vā purṣo va īti / mithyā-jñānaṃ viparyayaḥ / yathā śuktāv idaṃ rajatam iti / vyāpyā aropeṇa vyāpaka-āropas tarkaḥ yathā yadi vahnir na syāt tarhi dhūmo'pi na syād iti //

body.text: smṛtir api dvividhā / yathārthāyathārthā ca pramājanyā yathārthā / apramājanyāyathārthā //
body.translated_text: Memory (<s>smṛti</s>) too is of two kinds: veridical and non-veridical. That which is born from valid knowledge (<s>pramā</s>) is veridical; that which is born from invalid knowledge is non-veridical.

children.text: smṛtir api dvividhā / yathā-artha-ayathā-arthā ca pramā-janyā yathā-arthā / apramā-janya ā-yathā-arthā //

body.text: sarveśām anukūlatayā vedanīyaṃ sukham //
body.translated_text: <s>Sukha</s> (pleasure) is that which is experienced by all as agreeable.

children.text: sarveśām anukūlatayā vedanīyaṃ sukham //

body.text: sarveśāṃ pratikūlatayā vedanīyaṃ duḥkham //
body.translated_text: <s>Duḥkha</s> (pain) is that which is experienced by all as disagreeable.

children.text: sarveśāṃ pratikūlatayā vedanīyaṃ duḥkham //

body.text: icchā kāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: Desire (<s>icchā</s>) is <s>kāma</s> (longing).

children.text: icchā kāmaḥ //

body.text: krodho dveṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Anger (<s>krodha</s>) is <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion).

children.text: krodho dveṣaḥ //

body.text: kṛtiḥ prayatnaḥ //
body.translated_text: Effort (<s>kṛti</s>) is <s>prayatna</s> (volition).

children.text: kṛtiḥ prayatnaḥ //

body.text: vihitakarmajanyo dharmaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (merit) is that which arises from prescribed actions.

children.text: vihita-karma-janyo dharmaḥ //

body.text: niṣiddhakarmajanyas tv adharmaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Adharma</s> (demerit), however, is that which arises from prohibited actions.

children.text: niṣiddha-karma-janyas tv adharmaḥ //

body.text: buddhyādayo'ṣṭāv ātmamātraviśeṣaguṇāḥ //
body.translated_text: Cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) and the other eight [qualities] are qualities that belong exclusively to the <s>ātman</s> (self).

children.text: buddhy-ādayo'ṣṭāv ātma-mātraviśeṣa-guṇāḥ //

body.text: buddhīcchāprayatnā dvividhāḥ / nityā anityāś ca / nityā īśvarasya / anityā jīvasya //
body.translated_text: Cognition, desire, and effort are of two kinds: eternal and non-eternal. The eternal [ones belong] to <s>Īśvara</s> (God); the non-eternal to the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul).

children.text: buddhi-icchā-prayatnā dvividhāḥ / nityā anityāś ca / nityā īśvarasya / anityā jīvasya //

body.text: saṃskāras trividhaḥ / vego bhāvanā sthitisthāpakaś ceti / vegaḥ pṛthivyādicatuṣṭayamanovṛttiḥ / anubhavajanyā smṛtihetur bhāvanātmamātravṛttiḥ / anyathā kṛtasya punas tadavasthāpādakaḥ sthitisthāpakaḥ kaṭādipṛthivīvṛttiḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃskāra</s> (dispositional tendency) is of three kinds: <s>vega</s> (velocity), <s>bhāvanā</s> (impression), and <s>sthitisthāpaka</s> (elasticity). <s>Vega</s> is a property (<s>vṛtti</s>) residing in the four [substances] beginning with earth and in mind. <s>Bhāvanā</s>, born from experience and the cause of memory, is a property residing exclusively in the <s>ātman</s>. <s>Sthitisthāpaka</s> (elasticity), which restores to its original state something that has been displaced, is a property residing in earth-substances such as a mat, etc.

children.text: saṃskāras trividhaḥ / vego bhāvanā sthiti-sthāpakaś ca iti / vegaḥ pṛthivy-ādi-catuṣṭaya-mano-vṛttiḥ / anubhava-janyā smṛti-hetur bhāvanā ātma-mātra-vṛttiḥ / anyathā kṛtasya punas tad-avasthā-pādakaḥ sthiti-sthāpakaḥ kaṭa-ādi-pṛthivī-vṛttiḥ //

body.text: calanātmakaṃ karma / ūrdhvadeśasaṃyogahetur utkṣepaṇam / adhodeśasaṃyogahetur apakṣepaṇam / śarīrasaṃnikṛṣṭasaṃyogahetur ākuñcanam / viprakṛṣṭasaṃyogahetuḥ prasāraṇam / anyat sarvaṃ gamanam / pṛthivyādicatuṣṭayamanomātravṛtti //
body.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> (motion) is that whose nature is movement. Upward throwing (<s>utkṣepaṇa</s>) is that which causes conjunction with a higher location. Downward throwing (<s>apakṣepaṇa</s>) is that which causes conjunction with a lower location. Contraction (<s>ākuñcana</s>) is that which causes conjunction with [a place] near the body. Expansion (<s>prasāraṇa</s>) is that which causes conjunction with a distant [place]. All other [motion] is locomotion (<s>gamana</s>). [Motion] resides only in the four [substances] beginning with earth and in mind.

children.text: calana-ātmakaṃ karma / ūrdhva-deśa-saṃyoga-hetur utkṣepaṇam / adho-deśa-saṃyoga-hetur apakṣepaṇam / śarīra-saṃnikṛṣṭa-saṃyoga-hetur ākuñcanam / viprakṛṣṭa-saṃyoga-hetuḥ prasāraṇam / anyat sarvaṃ gamanam / pṛthivy-ādi-catuṣṭaya-mano-mātra-vṛtti //

body.text: nityam ekam anekānugataṃ sāmānyam / dravyaguṇakarmavṛtti / tad dvividhaṃ parāparabhedāt / paraṃ sattā / aparaṃ dravyatvādiḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Sāmānya</s> (universal) is that which is eternal, one, and present in many [instances]. It resides in substances, qualities, and motions. It is of two kinds, being divided into higher (<s>para</s>) and lower (<s>apara</s>). The highest is <s>sattā</s> (being/existence). The lower are <s>dravyatva</s> (substance-ness) and the like.

children.text: nityam ekam aneka-anugataṃ sāmānyam / dravya-guṇa-karma-vṛtti / tad dvividhaṃ para-apara-bhedāt / paraṃ sattā / aparaṃ dravyatva-ādiḥ //

body.text: nityadravyavṛttayo vyāvartakā viśeṣāḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Viśeṣas</s> (particularities) are the differentiators residing in eternal substances.

children.text: nitya-dravya-vṛttayo vyāvartakā viśeṣāḥ //

body.text: nityasaṃbandhaḥ samavāyaḥ / ayutasiddhavṛttiḥ / yayor dvayor madhya ekam avinaśyadaparāśritam evāvatiṣṭate tāv ayutasiddau / yathāvayavāvayavinau guṇaguṇinau kriyākriyāvantau jātivyaktī viśeṣanityadravye ceti //
body.translated_text: <s>Samavāya</s> (inherence) is an eternal relation. It resides in things that are <s>ayutasiddha</s> (inseparably connected). Two things are <s>ayutasiddha</s> when, of the two, one — while the other does not perish — exists only as dependent on the other. For example: part and whole, quality and quality-bearer, action and action-possessor, universal and individual, and particularity and eternal substance.

children.text: nitya-saṃbandhaḥ samavāyaḥ / ayuta-siddha-vṛttiḥ / yayor dvayor madhya ekam avinaśyad-apara-āśritam eva avatiṣṭate tāv ayutasiddau / yatha āvayava-avayavinau guṇa-guṇinau kriyā-kriyāvantau jāti-vyaktī viśeṣa-nitya-dravye ca iti //

body.text: anādiḥ sāntaḥ prāgabhāvaḥ / utpatteḥ pūrvaṃ kāryasya / sādir anantaḥ pradhvaṃsaḥ / utpattyanantaraṃ kāryasya / traikālikasaṃsargāvacchinnapratiyogitāko'tyantābhāvaḥ / yathā bhūtale ghaṭo nāstīti / tādātmyasaṃbandhāvacchinnapratiyogitāko'nyonyābhāvaḥ yathā ghaṭaḥ paṭo na bhavatīti //
body.translated_text: <s>Prāgabhāva</s> (prior absence) is beginningless and has an end — [it is the absence] of an effect before its origination. <s>Pradhvaṃsa</s> (posterior absence) has a beginning and no end — [it is the absence] of an effect after its destruction. <s>Atyantābhāva</s> (absolute absence) is that whose counter-correlate is qualified by relatedness to all three times — for example, 'There is no pot on the ground.' <s>Anyonyābhāva</s> (mutual absence) is that whose counter-correlate is qualified by the relation of identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) — for example, 'A pot is not a cloth.'

children.text: an-ādiḥ sa-antaḥ prāg-abhāvaḥ / utpatteḥ pūrvaṃ kāryasya / sa-ādir an-antaḥ pradhvaṃsaḥ / utpatty-an-antaraṃ kāryasya / traikālika-saṃsarga-avacchinna-pratiyogitāko'tyanta-abhāvaḥ / yathā bhūtale ghaṭo na asti iti / tādātmya-saṃbandha-avacchinna-pratiyogitāko'nyonya-abhāvaḥ yathā ghaṭaḥ paṭo na bhavati iti //

body.text: sarveṣāṃ padārthānāṃ yathāyatham ukteṣv antarbhāvāt saptaiva padārthā iti siddham //
body.translated_text: Since all [things] can be appropriately included within the [categories] stated, it is established that there are exactly seven categories (<s>padārtha</s>).

children.text: sarveṣāṃ pada-arthānāṃ yathā-yatham ukteṣv antarbhāvāt sapta eva pada-arthā iti siddham //
kāṇādanyāyamatayor bālāvyutpattisiddhaye /
children.translated_text: For the instruction of beginners in the doctrines of the <s>Kaṇāda</s> (Vaiśeṣika) and <s>Nyāya</s> systems,

children.text: annaṃbhaṭṭena viduṣā racitas tarkasaṃgrahaḥ //
children.translated_text: this <s>Tarkasaṃgraha</s> was composed by the learned <s>Annaṃbhaṭṭa</s>.

children.text: kāṇāda-nyāya-matayor bālā-vyutpatti-siddhaye /
annaṃbhaṭṭena viduṣā racitas tarkasaṃgrahaḥ //
